# M4 parity fixture provenance

`reference.js` is a dependency-free transcription of the pinned
`tensorResizeBilinear` and `tensorHWCtoBCHW` functions in
`projects/javascript/background-removal-js/packages/node/src/utils.ts` at
source commit `12f56cc4f2a90d624e165a715748d22efc7a1d93`. It is the sole
parity-artifact generator, not a Rust oracle. The canonical command first runs
the Rust runtime test with `M4_RUST_RAW_BIN` pointing at a temporary raw
output, then runs this generator with `M4_ARTIFACT_DIR` pointing at this
directory and redirects stdout to `parity.json`:

```sh
ORT_DYLIB=/private/tmp/bgremove-m4-runtime/onnxruntime-osx-arm64-1.23.2/lib/libonnxruntime.1.23.2.dylib \
M4_RUST_RAW_BIN=/private/tmp/m4-generated/rust-landscape.raw.f32le \
  cargo test -p bgremove-ort --offline --locked m4_real_fp32_cpu_parity_when_runtime_is_supplied -- --ignored
M4_NODE_ORT=/private/tmp/bgremove-m4-node/package \
M4_MODEL=$PWD/projects/javascript/background-removal-js/bundle/models/isnet \
M4_ARTIFACT_DIR=$PWD/tests/fixtures/m4 \
M4_RUST_RAW_BIN=/private/tmp/m4-generated/rust-landscape.raw.f32le \
  node tests/fixtures/m4/reference.js > tests/fixtures/m4/parity.json
```

Running the second command again into a temporary file and comparing it with
`cmp` must succeed byte-for-byte.

The checked-in fixture records decoded RGBA bytes and full tensor hashes for
landscape, portrait, and odd-sized edge/ramp images. The landscape full input
tensor is tracked as `reference-landscape.tensor.f32le` (12,582,912 bytes;
SHA-256 `406348a9ead28b8ee1e72d6def88231f7779d70e658dfadd1f975f381703327f`)
and the full model output as `reference-landscape.raw.f32le` (4,194,304
bytes; SHA-256 `1fe02354161ace92e06be71241c88d70ecca60ab8c14ed023031bfd3f688dfed`).
The three tiny `*.straight-alpha-cutout.rgba` files preserve the complete
straight-alpha bytes. All are generated by the real FP32 model using
`onnxruntime-node@1.21.0`; Rust CPU 1.23.2 compares every landscape tensor
value and raw value within the recorded tolerances. The real model files are
verified by the M4 manifests before session creation.

`rembg-pillow-fixture.json` is generated by
`generate_rembg_pillow_fixture.py` with the pinned development-only
Pillow `10.4.0` environment. It records the source ramp, Pillow LANCZOS
resized bytes, global-maximum normalization evidence, min/max mask bytes, and
restored bytes. Rust's image-crate Lanczos3 is compared against it with the
recorded measured limits (input max/mean 5/0.3173 u8; normalized max
0.019607849214591244 and mean 0.0012442842930558472 f32, enforced at
0.019608/0.001245); this is an explicit compatibility bound rather than a
claim of Pillow byte identity.
